stem: A nursing student compares the common forms of spina bifida. Which statement correctly distinguishes myelomeningocele?

options.A: A sac protrudes through the spinal defect and contains part of the spinal cord and nerves
options.B: Only the meninges and cerebrospinal fluid protrude, with no spinal cord in the sac
options.C: The vertebral defect is covered by skin and the spinal cord and meninges do not protrude
options.D: The condition is an acquired spinal disorder that develops after birth

rationale: CDC describes myelomeningocele as the most serious common form of spina bifida: a fluid-filled sac protrudes through an opening in the back and contains part of the spinal cord and nerves, which can be damaged. Meningocele contains meninges/CSF without the spinal cord in the sac, while spina bifida occulta is a closed vertebral defect without protrusion of the cord or meninges. Spina bifida is a congenital neural-tube defect, not an acquired postnatal disorder. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Differentiate myelomeningocele from meningocele and spina bifida occulta by recognizing that the myelomeningocele sac contains spinal cord and neural tissue.
